step-1.text: Stand one side panel on its edge, holes facing in. Screw in four cam pins by hand, then tap in four dowels.

count-1.text: This step uses 1 side panel, 4 cam pins and 4 wood dowels.

step-2.text: Slide the bottom panel onto the pins at the low end. Two cam locks go in, arrow toward the pin, then a firm clockwise turn.

count-2.text: This step uses 1 bottom panel and 2 cam locks.

step-3.text: The fixed shelf holds the frame square, so it goes in now. Slide onto the pins and lock with cam locks, clockwise.

count-3.text: This step uses 1 fixed shelf and 2 cam locks.

step-4.text: Tap dowels into the panel below, then press the divider down onto them. Dowels go in the top end too, ready for what sits above.

count-4.text: This step uses 1 divider and 4 wood dowels.

step-5.text: Pins and dowels go into the ends of the panels on this side too. Lower the second side onto all of them at once, then lock the last four cam locks.

count-5.text: This step uses 1 side panel, 4 cam pins, 4 wood dowels and 4 cam locks.

step-6.text: Tap four dowels into the top edges of the sides. Set the top panel on, good side up, then lock it from inside with four cam locks.

count-6.text: This step uses 1 top panel, 4 wood dowels and 4 cam locks.

step-7.text: Tip the frame onto its front, on a rug or the flattened box so nothing gets scratched.

count-7.text: Nothing new this step. Just you and the frame.

step-8.text: Lay the back panel on, smooth side facing in. Line it up with one corner and nail it along the edges, about every twenty centimeters. If the corners line up, the frame is square.

step-9.text: While it lies on its front, twist a leg into each corner of the bottom. Hand tight, then a quarter turn more.

step-10.text: Stand it back up on its feet. Nice, the box is done.

count-10.text: Nothing new this step. Just you and the frame.

step-11.text: Runner time. Four pairs, one on each wall of every opening, screwed into the pre-drilled holes. Left and right runners are mirror images, so check the labels.

count-11.text: This step uses 8 drawer runners and 16 screws.

step-12.text: First drawer. Lay the drawer front face down on something soft. Tap in four dowels, then press both drawer sides onto them, grooves facing in.

count-12.text: This step uses 1 small drawer front, 2 drawer sides and 4 wood dowels.

step-13.text: The drawer bottom slides into the grooves from the back. Shiny side up. Push it home against the front.

step-14.text: Close the drawer with its back panel, then drive four screws through the back into the sides. Snug, not cranked.

count-14.text: This step uses 1 drawer back and 4 screws.

step-15.text: Now the other three drawers, exactly the same way: front, sides, bottom, back. Then slide every drawer in onto its runners until it stops. The demo leaves drawer one pulled open so you can see inside. Take a break halfway if you need one.

count-15.text: This step uses 1 small drawer front, 6 drawer sides, 3 drawer bottoms, 3 drawer backs, 2 drawer fronts, 12 wood dowels and 12 screws.

step-16.text: One knob per drawer. Each one gets a screw from the inside of the drawer front. Hand tight is plenty.

step-17.text: Fix the wall bracket to the back edge of the top, then into the wall with fixings made for your wall type. Tip-overs are real. Anchor it.

done.text: Done. Your WILLOW 4-drawer dresser is built. Give it a proud little pat.
